mainTopic: Twin firstborn animals, and whether people can measure with perfect precision (צמצום) according to the רבנן
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about twin firstborn animals. It covers the priestly gifts from the doubtful twin, what happens if one twin dies, and the case of a male and a female twin. Then the גמרא asks a new question. רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that perfect precision (צמצום) is possible even in things Heaven controls. The רבנן hold it is impossible there. But what do the רבנן hold about things people do on purpose? The גמרא tries several proofs: the red line around the מזבח, the exact measurements of the vessels, a clay vessel broken into equal halves, and רבי אליעזר's ruling about a body found exactly between two towns. Each of the first three proofs is pushed away. The rejection of the last proof begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The doubtful twin still owes the priestly gifts
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the animal in doubt is obligated in מתנות when slaughtered. רבי יוסי exempts it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is obligated in the priestly gifts, and רבי יוסי exempts it.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the משנה in the middle. It is finishing its rule about the twin that stays with the owner because we are not sure which one is the בכור. When that twin is slaughtered, the owner must give the regular gifts to the כהן, but רבי יוסי says he does not have to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular animal that is not sacred owes the כהן three gifts: the foreleg, the jaws, and the stomach. The first opinion says this doubtful animal is treated like a regular animal for this purpose. רבי יוסי says it is exempt, but the משנה does not give his reason here.

keyTerms.meaning: The priestly gifts (foreleg, jaws, stomach) taken from a regular slaughtered animal
Obligated
Exempts

phrases.english: And he is obligated in the priestly gifts,
phrases.notes: He is talking about the twin that stayed with the owner because of the doubt.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yosei exempts him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous page about twin firstborns.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The doubtful twin owes the priestly gifts; רבי יוסי exempts it.

steps.title: If one twin died: split it, or the owner keeps it
steps.stepSummary: If one of the two twins died, רבי טרפון says the כהן and the owner split the one that is left. רבי עקיבא says the one who wants to take it must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of them died, רבי טרפון says they divide it. רבי עקיבא says the one who wants to take from his friend must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new case: one twin died, and we do not know if the dead one was the בכור. רבי טרפון says the owner and the כהן split the living one. רבי עקיבא says the owner keeps it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions deal with real doubt about who owns the living twin. רבי טרפון solves it by dividing. רבי עקיבא uses the general money rule: the animal is in the owner's hands, so the כהן cannot take it unless he proves it is his.

keyTerms.meaning: They divide it
The one who wants to take from another person must bring the proof

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule הַמּוֹצִיא מֵחֲבֵירוֹ עָלָיו הָרְאָיָה is a basic rule for money cases across all of ש״ס.

phrases.english: If one of them died —
Rabbi Tarfon says: they divide it,
phrases.notes: The כהן and the owner split the twin that is still alive.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
The one who takes from his fellow, the proof is upon him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case within the same משנה about twins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי טרפון: they divide. רבי עקיבא: the owner keeps it, because the claimant must bring proof.

steps.title: A male and a female twin: the priest gets nothing
steps.stepSummary: If a male and a female were born together, the כהן gets nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a male and a female were born, the כהן has nothing here.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last case in the משנה. If the twins were a male and a female, the כהן gets nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a male can be a בכור. We do not know if the female came out first. If she did, she already opened the womb, and the male is not a בכור. Because of this doubt, the כהן cannot claim the male.

keyTerms.meaning: A male and a female
The priest has nothing here

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה is about twins born from a first birth. Whether it is even possible for two babies to come out at the exact same moment is what sets up the גמרא's question.

phrases.english: A male and a female —
the priest has nothing here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final case of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a male and a female twin, the כהן has no claim.

steps.title: Can people measure exactly, according to the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי notes that רבי יוסי הגלילי says perfect precision is possible, even in Heaven's hands. They ask what the רבנן hold about precision in human hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי said: We heard that רבי יוסי הגלילי holds precision is possible in Heaven's hands, and all the more so in human hands. The רבנן hold it is impossible in Heaven's hands. But what do they hold about human hands?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and opens a new question. It wants to know whether the רבנן think a person can measure or act with perfect precision. The next steps will try to answer this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יוסי הגלילי says both twins can come out at the exact same moment, so he holds צמצום is possible, even in Heaven's hands. If so, it is surely possible when a person is trying to be exact. The רבנן say twins cannot come out at the exact same moment, which only tells us their view on things Heaven controls. Things people control are still an open question.

keyTerms.meaning: To be perfectly exact, so two things match precisely
In the hands of Heaven, meaning things people do not control
In human hands, meaning things people do on purpose
All the more so
What is the answer?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the רבנן clearly hold that people cannot be exact. The משנה only shows their view about Heaven's hands. Their view about human hands is exactly what the גמרא is asking.
steps.whyThisMatters: The question of צמצום comes up in many places in ש״ס, so knowing where each side stands is important.

phrases.english: GEMARA
They said in the school of Rabbi Yannai:
Regarding Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, we have heard him
phrases.notes: From the earlier part of our משנה, where he says both twins go to the כהן.

phrases.english: that he says it is possible to be precise in the hands of Heaven,
and all the more so in human hands,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן — בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם,
phrases.english: and the Rabbis — in the hands of Heaven it is impossible to be precise,
in human hands, what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the dispute in the משנה to raise a wider question about precision.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the רבנן hold that perfect precision is possible when people do something on purpose?

steps.title: Proof from the red line around the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: A red line ran around the middle of the מזבח to separate the upper bloods from the lower bloods. If people could not mark the exact middle, blood would sometimes be put in the wrong place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A red line went around the middle of the מזבח to separate the upper bloods from the lower bloods. If you say people cannot be exact, sometimes he would put upper blood below and lower blood above!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove that the רבנן agree people can be exact. It uses the red line around the middle of the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some blood must go above the middle of the מזבח and some must go below it. The line is supposed to mark the exact middle. If people could not measure exactly, the line would be a bit off, and the כהן might put blood in the wrong half. Since the הלכה relies on this line to separate the two halves, it seems people can measure exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, which introduces a proof
The red line painted around the מזבח
Blood that must be placed on the upper half of the מזבח
Blood that must be placed on the lower half of the מזבח

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A red line encircles it in the middle,
phrases.notes: "It" is the מזבח. This comes from a משנה describing the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: to separate between the upper bloods
and the lower bloods.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם בִּידֵי אָדָם,
phrases.english: And if you say it is impossible to be precise in human hands,
sometimes he would put the upper ones below
phrases.notes: "He" is the כהן placing the blood.

phrases.english: and the lower ones above!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: חוּט שֶׁל סִיקְרָא חוֹגְרוֹ בָּאֶמְצַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן hold people can be exact.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about the red line around the middle of the מזבח.

steps.title: The line was made a little wider
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away: they made the line a bit thick, so it surely covers the true middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the red-line proof. The line was made a little wide, so no exact measurement was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the line is thick enough, the true middle is somewhere inside it even if nobody knows the exact spot. The כהן puts upper blood above the line and lower blood below it, so he can never be in the wrong half. The line does not show that people can be perfectly exact.

keyTerms.meaning: He widens it
A little

phrases.english: That he widens it a little.
phrases.notes: The line is made thick enough that the real middle is surely somewhere inside it.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the red-line proof is rejected; the question stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A wide line works without exact measurement, so it proves nothing about precision.

steps.title: Proof from the exact sizes of the vessels and the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries another proof: the תורה gives exact measurements for the כלים and the מזבח, so people must be able to measure exactly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear from the measurements of the vessels, from the measurement of the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second proof. The תורה gives exact sizes for the משכן vessels and the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה commands exact sizes, people must be able to build them exactly. Otherwise the command could not be kept. This suggests that precision in human hands is possible.

keyTerms.meaning: The measurements of the משכן and מקדש vessels
The altar

phrases.english: Come and hear from the measurement of the vessels,
from the measurement of the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new proof after the first one was rejected.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן hold people can be exact.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The exact measurements the תורה gives for the vessels and the מזבח.

steps.title: Doing your best is enough there
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away: for the vessels, the תורה only asks us to do our best, and ה׳ is pleased with that. A פסוק supports this.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the תורה said 'make it,' and however you are able to make it is pleasing to Him: 'All this in writing, from the hand of ה׳ upon me, He made me understand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second proof. With the vessels, the תורה only asks for our best effort, so it does not prove that people can be perfectly exact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The command to build the vessels does not need perfect precision. Building them as well as you can is enough, and ה׳ accepts it. So the exact measurements do not prove that perfect precision is possible, and the גמרא keeps looking for a proof in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there
The Merciful One, meaning ה׳ or the תורה
Do it, make it
It is pleasing to Him

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs that people can be exact were pushed away. The red line was made wide, and for the vessels the תורה only wants our best effort.

phrases.english: It is different there,
because the Merciful One said: Make it,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְכֹל הֵיכִי דְּמָצֵית לְמִיעְבַּד נִיחָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: and in whatever way you are able to make it, it is pleasing to Him,
"All this in writing, from the hand of the Lord upon me, He made me understand."
phrases.notes: This is a פסוק in דברי הימים, where דוד describes the plans for the בית המקדש.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the measurements of the vessels and the מזבח is rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: For the vessels, ה׳ only asks for our best effort, so the exact sizes do not show that perfect precision is possible.

steps.title: Proof from a clay vessel broken into equal halves
steps.stepSummary: רב קטינא cites a ברייתא: if an impure clay vessel is broken into two equal pieces, both stay impure, because exact precision is impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב קטינא said: Come and hear. If someone broke an impure clay vessel into two pieces of the same size, both pieces stay impure, because it is impossible to be exactly precise.
steps.whatsHappening: רב קטינא brings a new proof that people cannot measure with perfect precision.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A broken impure clay vessel normally works like this: the bigger piece stays impure and the smaller piece becomes pure. If the two pieces really could be exactly equal, the law would need a special ruling for that case. Instead the ברייתא says both pieces are impure 'because it is impossible to be exact.' That sounds like a clear statement that human precision is impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source as proof
A clay (earthenware) vessel
He divided it into two pieces
To be exactly precise, to match perfectly
Ritually impure (plural)

phrases.english: Rav Ketina said: Come and hear:
If one divided it into two, and they are equal,
phrases.notes: 'It' is an impure clay oven or vessel. Normally, when it breaks, the bigger piece stays impure and the smaller one becomes pure.

phrases.english: both of them are impure,
because it is impossible to be exactly precise.
phrases.notes: We can never be sure they are truly equal, so one of them is probably a bit bigger and still impure. Since we don't know which one, both are treated as impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the כלים was pushed away in step 8, a new proof is brought.
steps.raayaObject: That, according to the רבנן, perfect precision is impossible in human hands.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about breaking an impure clay vessel into two equal pieces.

steps.title: Clay is different because its edges are jagged
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא rejects the proof: a clay vessel has uneven pits and bumps where it breaks, so it cannot be measured exactly. This tells us nothing about measuring in general.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: A clay vessel is different, because it has pits and dents in it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא pushes away רב קטינא's proof by saying clay is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The broken edge of a clay vessel is rough and full of dents, so its exact size can never be known. That is why the ברייתא says precision is impossible there. Smooth, ordinary things might still be measured exactly, so the general question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different: this case is special
Since, because
Pits, dents, uneven spots

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
A clay vessel is different,
since it has dents in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: שָׁאנֵי כְּלִי חֶרֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the ברייתא to clay vessels only. It does not show that human precision is impossible in general.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The impossibility comes from the clay's uneven surface, not from a general rule about human precision.

steps.title: A body found exactly between two towns
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites רבי אליעזר: if a murdered person is found exactly between two towns, each town brings its own עגלה ערופה. Then it asks for his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if the body was found exactly between two towns, both towns bring two heifers. These are the words of רבי אליעזר. What is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source about עגלה ערופה and asks why רבי אליעזר rules this way. It is setting up the proof that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally only the one town nearest to the body brings an עגלה ערופה. רבי אליעזר says that if the body lies exactly in the middle, both towns bring one. The question 'what is the reason?' prepares the inference that people must be able to measure exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: The heifer whose neck is broken when a murdered person is found and the killer is unknown
Exactly, precisely in line
Towns
What is the reason?

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If it was found exactly between two towns,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the body of a murdered person, the case of עגלה ערופה.

phrases.english: both of them bring two heifers,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: נִמְצָא מְכוּוָּן בֵּין שְׁתֵּי עֲיָירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the clay-vessel proof was rejected, a new source is brought.
steps.raayaObject: That perfect precision is possible in human hands.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר's ruling on עגלה ערופה (משנה in סוטה).

steps.title: Suggested reason: people can measure exactly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רבי אליעזר's reason: people can measure exactly, and the פסוק's word 'nearest' can mean two equally near towns.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it because he holds that in human hands exact precision is possible? And 'the nearest' town can include even two nearest towns?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the proof: רבי אליעזר's ruling only makes sense if people can measure exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two towns can only both be 'nearest' if we can know for sure that they are exactly the same distance away. That requires perfect human measuring. If exact measuring were impossible, one town would always really be closer. Then they would bring one heifer together instead of two.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not because...? (the start of a suggested reason)
He holds, he is of the opinion
In human hands: done by people
'Nearest': the word in the פסוק about the town that brings the heifer

phrases.english: Is it not because he holds
that in human hands it is possible to be exactly precise,
and 'nearest' means even two nearest ones?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּקָסָבַר בִּידֵי אָדָם אֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'what is the reason' of step 11 and draws the proof out of it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An inference from רבי אליעזר's ruling that two towns bring two heifers.

steps.title: The rejection begins: No, רבי אליעזר...
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to push away the proof from רבי אליעזר. The rest of the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says 'no' and begins to give a different reason for רבי אליעזר's ruling. The full answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'no' tells us the proof from step 12 will be rejected. The גמרא is about to explain רבי אליעזר's ruling in a way that does not depend on people measuring exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: No: a signal that a proof is being pushed away
The תנא whose ruling is being re-explained

phrases.english: No, Rabbi Eliezer...
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next amud, where the גמרא gives another reason for his ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins rejecting the inference of step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Aims to show that רבי אליעזר's ruling does not prove that human precision is possible. The details continue on the next amud.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There may be another reason for רבי אליעזר's ruling. It is explained in the continuation.
